messages:
Alex: Quick check — does /v1/usage (hosted) return separate fields for prompt vs completion vs cached tokens? We're trying to reconcile billing with accounting. Draft proposal: `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `charged_tokens`. Any compatibility concerns? cc @Jin @Maria

Jin: We currently return `input_tokens` and `output_tokens`. Adding new fields is fine but we should keep the old names as aliases for at least one release to avoid breaking customers. Also, streaming vs final totals question — prefer only final totals in the response body.

Maria: Accounting needs a clear, unambiguous definition for each field. `charged_tokens` is required for reconciliation (what we actually bill). Cached handling: we treat cached tokens as free. Edge cases: KV cache re-use across requests and multi-turn sessions. Need to know whether `cached_tokens` counts prompt-only cache or both prompt+completion.

Alex: Proposal details: flat fields (no nested object) — `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `cached_prompt_tokens`, `cached_completion_tokens`, `cached_tokens` (sum), and `charged_tokens`. Also include `billing_version` e.g. `v2` to signal schema changes. For compatibility: emit `input_tokens`=`prompt_tokens` and `output_tokens`=`completion_tokens` until next major.

Sam: For streaming endpoints — the client needs incremental tokens sometimes, but for billing we only need final counts. Suggest: stream partial token counts in `x-stream-tokens` headers but final body always contains canonical fields. Keep header change lightweight.

Jin: Makes sense. Also: rounding rules — we should document that tokens are integers and server-side uses ceil() on fractional sub-token accounting (e.g., partial byte groups). Will add to spec.

AccountingBot: Quick note — charged_tokens must be an integer and represent billable tokens after discounts/credits applied. Cached tokens must be explicitly excluded from charged_tokens. For reconciliation tests we need sample payloads showing: cache-hit (true), cache-miss, partial-cache.

Maria: Can we add a `cache_hit` boolean and `cache_origin` string (e.g., "kv-prefix", "model-cache")? That would help tie traces back to cache metrics. If we keep flat fields, `cache_hit` is fine.

Alex: Updated minimal suggested schema (final response):

```json
{
  "prompt_tokens": 12,
  "completion_tokens": 38,
  "cached_tokens": 5,
  "cached_prompt_tokens": 3,
  "cached_completion_tokens": 2,
  "charged_tokens": 45,
  "cache_hit": false,
  "billing_version": "v2",
  "input_tokens": 12,        // deprecated alias
  "output_tokens": 38        // deprecated alias
}
```

Alex: We'll keep the aliases for one release, emit deprecation warning in release notes and docs. I'll open a PR with schema + migration plan.

Jin: Tests: add unit tests for corner cases: 0-length prompts, completion-only calls, full cache hit (charged_tokens == 0), and cross-request KV cache reuse (ensure cached_tokens counts only reused tokens).

Maria: I can own reconciler test vectors. Please include examples where cached prompt tokens are split across requests (session reuse) — accounting needs to attribute cached tokens to the later request that benefited.

Alex: Filing PR in ~2h: will tag `api/billing-v2` and add changelog. Will also ping eng-docs to update the public API docs.

DeployBot: PR #424 opened: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/424 — CI started.

Sam: Ack. Will review the PR later today. :thumbsup:

AccountingBot: FYI I've set up a quick spreadsheet template to reconcile sample responses with invoices. Will share in #finance after PR merges.

Alex: Thanks everyone — will post the PR link here when CI passes and add a canary rollout plan for Dedicated first.

Jin: One more: add `billing_region` string? Some customers need per-region accounting. Optional field ok.

Alex: Good call — adding optional `billing_region` to the schema.

Maria: Great. I'll start drafting reconciliation tests now.

Sam: cool.
